MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves is the new roadmap proposed by PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24 (route 1, accepted by its review) with the same id, title ('Tautological rings and motivic structures in the cohomology of moduli of stable curves') and area; DESIGN-MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves is pending, and its brief already asks for 'the vanishing of the low-degree Borel–Moore homology of M_{g,n} proved by Bergström–Faber–Payne'. The atlas has no moduli of curves, so the 49 moduli-theoretic items belong there. The brief lists the final theorems and imports the point-counting tools from WeilConjectures, the weight spectral sequence from DWP.8 and the elementary lemmas from FF and GN.

Accept. WC.1 plans the zeta function's disjoint-union and open–closed factorizations and consumes the determinant formula; Behrend's stack point counts, the Vakil–Wood inverse-zeta formula and the Hasse–Weil sieve are extensions of exactly that interface. WC.2 owns Poincaré duality, WC.4 the Betti comparison in families, and WC.5:power-sum-converse is the finite-spectrum lemma that van den Bogaart–Edixhoven's Lemma 4.1 is. All five stage ids resolve.

Accept. DWP.8 owns weight filtrations of mixed ℓ-adic complexes; the Galois-equivariant weight spectral sequence of a normal crossings compactification is its geometric instance. The stage id resolves.

Accept. FF.1 plans characters and elementary sums (the quadratic-character correlation by interpolation) and FF.3 polynomial factorization and point counting (the squarefree count via f = h·m²). Both stage ids resolve.

Accept. GN.2 integrates the classification of quadratic forms by discriminant and local invariants 'with characteristic restrictions'; the three PGL₄(F_q)-orbits of reduced irreducible quadric surfaces and their automorphism orders are its finite-field case. The stage id resolves.
